decisions.diagnosis: The southbound piezo lost sensitivity through the 2019 cool season: it went nearly silent in the cold early-morning and evening hours while northbound counted normally, and had intermittent full dropouts only in this direction, so southbound weekly totals are undercounted.
decisions.evidence: Weekly S/N ratio for 05-09h fell abruptly from 0.9-1.2 (Apr 2019) to 0.08-0.56 from week 2019-04-29 to late Sep (2018 same weeks 0.67-1.22; 2020 0.8-2.2); weekday 05-09h south 3-13 vs north 21-43 (e.g. 2019-04-29..05-03), whereas 2019-04-22..26 had 17-59 vs 23-47; monthly mean south 05-09h 6.7-12.7/day vs 14-24 in every other winter; zero_outage fired on south alone 9 times May-Sep 2019; midday S/N also depressed (1.34-1.8 vs ~2.0); recovery gradual through early Oct.

decisions.diagnosis: The same southbound sensor fault came back in the 2021 cool season: cold-hour counts collapsed and there were south-only partial dropouts, and TfNSW's site comment flags MetroCount issues from 16/07/21 to 13/08/21.
decisions.evidence: Weekday 05-09h south 1-9 vs north 21-41 from 2021-04-19 (13-15 Apr 11-22 vs 26-42; 5-9 Apr 18-37 vs 22-42); weekly 05-09h S/N 0.19-0.53 in most weeks and 17-20h S/N 0.24-1.3 (2020 same months 0.8-2.0 and 1.3-3.1); monthly south 05-09h 4.7-11.5/day vs 16-24 in 2020/2022-2026 winters; zero_outage south-only on 10 days May-Aug 2021; weekly total S/N 0.94-1.3 vs 1.4-2.1 around it; normal from 29 Sep (south 05-09h 29-30 vs north 9-13).

decisions.diagnosis: The first 9 days after installation (the first record is 15:00 on 19 Jul 2011) are far below the steady level in both directions; this could be commissioning or weather, and the data does not settle which.
decisions.evidence: North 3-7/day and south 4-16/day on 20-23 Jul, north 9-26 on 24-27 Jul; from 28 Jul north 41-104 and south 87-178; the commuter peaks appear gradually (north 7am 1 -> 12 -> 17 by 28 Jul).

summary: Site 112 (Captain Cook Bridge shared path) has one Metrocount piezo with two clean single-record directions from 2011 to 2026, with a gap from Oct 2021 to Aug 2022. The only fault is the southbound sensor losing counts in cold hours in the 2019 and 2021 cool seasons, which undercounts the southbound weekly totals; those periods are set to missing. The COVID surge in April 2020 and the annual March Sunday southbound ride spikes (up to about 1,200 in a day) are real and kept.
